caption:
You’ve seen me at games for months. Here’s what you didn’t see before I got there. Or when I sneak away.

About 6 months ago I started getting symptoms that didn’t make sense. Scary symptoms that fit the criteria of heart attacks. Dizzy out of nowhere. Heart pounding from my chest and racing for no reason. Pure adrenaline dumps that wake me to the point I cannot breathe. Exhausted in a way that sleep doesn’t fix.

After I cannot remember how many hospital trips, ambulance rides, more appointments, I finally got a piece of the puzzle (which I brought up to the dr): POTS. It’s a nervous system thing that messes with your heart rate and blood pressure, to name a tiny few symptoms.

Here’s the part that actually got me… standing for long periods is one of the things that makes it worse.

So the sidelines I’ve been standing on all season? Or trying to find a spot to sit so I can make it through a practice or game. Not just “tired mom” hard. Actually hard.

We’re still figuring out the rest of it. More appointments, more questions than answers some days. This isn’t my first rodeo with something nobody can see, but it’s the first time I’ve had a name for part of it.

If you’re in your own “still finding out” phase with something invisible, while knee deep in motherhood and sports mode, I see you. You don’t need a diagnosis to deserve support.

If something invisible is part of your story too, drop a 🤍 below. You don’t have to explain it.

caption:
Every wellness trend feels overdone until you realize “wellness” during the busy season just means protein pancakes for dinner and calling it a win.

Three questions I run everything through now:

• Does this actually fit a night where practice means we leave at 5 and ends at 8 and everyone’s starving.. or does it just look good on someone with a kitchen and a plan?

• What’s the version that works for ME, not the wellness girlies meal-prepping on a Sunday I don’t have?

• How do I want to feel feeding my family tonight, and not how “clean” does it have to look to count?

That’s the difference between wellness that survives sports season and wellness that quietly dies the second life gets full.

You don’t need a four-course dinner. You need protein, something they’ll actually eat, and five minutes.

Protein pancakes for dinner… genius or flop? 
Tell me I’m not the only one..

Anxiety has been hitting different lately with everything going on with my health. And I stumbled across this concept called a “nostalgic reset” and honestly… I wish I had seen this sooner.

The science is wild. When you listen to music tied to a specific memory, junior high, high school, that one summer… your brain releases dopamine AND oxytocin at the same time. That combo literally calms your nervous system down. Especially if you feel your mind spiralling.

It’s not living in the past. It’s called autobiographical memory recall. And researchers say it reduces loneliness, lowers cortisol, and gives you this feeling that your life actually makes sense.

I’ve been building my reset playlist and 10 minutes, no scrolling, just the music, it’s becoming my thing because you know this sport mom lives in her car.

caption:
Homemade Egg Nog! 

2 cups whole milk
1 cinnamon stick
1/2 tsp. ground nutmeg
1 tsp. pure vanilla extract
6 large egg yolks
1/2 cup cane sugar
1 cup heavy cream
1/4 tsp ground cinnamon for topping, optional !

We triple this recipe as we can go through quite a bit with a family of five who LOVES Egg Nog. It’s also a great way to use up 18 eggs and save the whites to makes some treats another day with the kids.

Directions:

Separate egg yolks in a bowl. 
Whisk in sugar until a pale yellow.
Bring milk, cinnamon sticks, vanilla and nutmeg to a low boil on stove and remove.
SLOWLY add milk to the egg mixture. Little bit at a time so you don’t cook the eggs.
Put the pot back on the stove and thicken until it sticks to the back of a spoon. 
Add the cream remove from heat and put in jars, then to the fridge for 7 hours. I sprinkle cinnamon on top before we close the lids.

Save this for later and skip the ones from the store.
